Cap salary outliers (quantile)

cap_outliers_salary.Rd

Handle extreme values (outliers) in a numeric column by replacing them with specified quantile cut-offs. This is a simple "winsorisation" strategy.

Usage

cap_outliers_salary(
  data,
  col = "salary_in_usd",
  lower = 0.01,
  upper = 0.99,
  clip_side = c("both", "upper", "lower"),
  na_rm = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame containing the data.

col

Character string. Name of the column to process (default "salary_in_usd").

lower

Probability for the lower quantile (between 0 and 1, default 0.01).

upper

Probability for the upper quantile (between 0 and 1, default 0.99).

clip_side

Capping strategy: "both" (default), "upper" or "lower".

na_rm

Logical. Should NA values be ignored when computing quantiles? (default TRUE)

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, prints a summary of the replacements performed.

Value

The data.frame with the target column modified (extreme values are replaced by the corresponding quantile bounds).

Details

The function computes two bounds, L (lower) and U (upper), corresponding to the requested quantile probabilities. Values below L are replaced by L, and values above U are replaced by U. You can choose whether to cap both tails, only the upper tail, or only the lower tail.

See also

Other Data quality: validate_ranges()

Examples

# Simple data with an extreme salary value (1 million)
df <- data.frame(
  salary_in_usd = c(50000, 55000, 60000, 45000, 1000000)
)

# Cap the upper 10% (winsorisation)
df_capped <- cap_outliers_salary(df, lower = 0.1, upper = 0.9, clip_side = "upper")
#> Error in cap_outliers_salary(df, lower = 0.1, upper = 0.9, clip_side = "upper"): could not find function "cap_outliers_salary"

# The value 1,000,000 is replaced by the 90th percentile
print(df_capped)
#> Error: object 'df_capped' not found
